look_here_first: Look for opposite long-petioled broad leaves with coarse teeth and three strong basal veins, topped by loose white flat-topped clusters of tiny all-disk heads—no ray florets.

project_inclusion.range_basis: USDA-derived county data explicitly marks Bandera, Comal, Kerr, Medina and Travis native; first three used for threshold.

best_field_traits: erect rhizomatous perennial of shaded/moist sites
opposite broadly ovate to triangular long-petioled leaves
leaves coarsely toothed with three strong veins from near base
terminal corymbiform clusters of many small white heads
heads discoid: white disk florets only, no rays
morphology_keys.leaf_morphology: Broadly ovate/triangular, coarsely toothed, commonly 3-veined from near base.
morphology_keys.heads: White discoid heads with no ray florets.
morphology_keys.reproductive_confirmation: Mature cypselae glabrous, not hispid, contrasted with A. havanensis (Flora of North America).

comparisons.key_distinctions: FNA: A. altissima is herbaceous, with larger usually long-petioled, coarsely double-toothed leaves and GLABROUS cypselae; A. havanensis has a persistent woody shrub framework, shorter-petioled generally smaller leaves, and HISPID cypselae. Chromolaena odorata shows much longer cylindrical involucres (8–10 mm) with 4–6+ phyllary series.
